sentences.c: 项脊轩，旧南阁子也。
sentences.m: 项脊轩，就是原来的南阁子。
sentences.e: The Xiangji Chamber was formerly the South Pavilion.

sentences.c: 室仅方丈，可容一人居。
sentences.m: 屋子只有一丈见方，只能容一个人居住。
sentences.e: The room was barely ten feet square, just enough for one person to live in.

sentences.c: 百年老屋，尘泥渗漉，雨泽下注；每移案，顾视无可置者。
sentences.m: 这是上百年的老屋，灰尘泥土往下漏，雨水也往下灌；每次挪动书桌，环顾四周都没有可以安放的地方。
sentences.e: It was a hundred-year-old house: dust and mud seeped through, and rainwater poured down; whenever I moved my desk, I looked about and found nowhere to put it.

sentences.c: 又北向，不能得日，日过午已昏。
sentences.m: 屋子又朝北，照不到阳光，一过中午天就暗了。
sentences.e: It faced north, so it got no sun, and by early afternoon it was already dim.

sentences.c: 余稍为修葺，使不上漏。
sentences.m: 我稍微加以修补，使它上面不再漏雨。
sentences.e: I made a few repairs so that it no longer leaked from above.

sentences.c: 前辟四窗，垣墙周庭，以当南日，日影反照，室始洞然。
sentences.m: 在前面开了四扇窗子，又砌墙围住院子，用来挡住南边的日光，日光反射过来，屋里才明亮起来。
sentences.e: I opened four windows at the front and built a wall around the courtyard to catch the southern sun; the light reflected back, and only then did the room become bright.

sentences.c: 又杂植兰桂竹木于庭，旧时栏楯，亦遂增胜。
sentences.m: 又在院中错杂地种上兰花、桂树、竹子和其他树木，旧日的栏杆，也因此增添了景致。
sentences.e: I also planted orchids, cassia, bamboo and other trees at random in the courtyard, and the old railings gained in beauty thereby.

sentences.c: 借书满架，偃仰啸歌，冥然兀坐，万籁有声；而庭阶寂寂，小鸟时来啄食，人至不去。
sentences.m: 借来的书摆满书架，我仰卧起坐、长啸高歌，或者静静地端坐着，听万种声响；而庭院台阶一片寂静，小鸟时常飞来啄食，人走近了也不飞走。
sentences.e: Borrowed books filled the shelves; I lay back and rose, whistled and sang, or sat still in silence while every sound of nature came through; and the courtyard steps were so quiet that small birds often came to peck, and did not fly off when I approached.

sentences.c: 三五之夜，明月半墙，桂影斑驳，风移影动，珊珊可爱。
sentences.m: 每月十五的夜晚，明月照亮半面墙，桂树的影子斑斑驳驳，风吹影动，轻盈美好，十分可爱。
sentences.e: On the nights of the full moon, bright light lay on half the wall, the cassia's shadow fell mottled and mixed, and as the wind moved the shadows swayed — delicate and lovely.

sentences.c: 然余居于此，多可喜，亦多可悲。
sentences.m: 然而我住在这里，有很多可喜的事，也有很多可悲的事。
sentences.e: Yet in living here I had much to rejoice in, and much to grieve over.

sentences.c: 先是庭中通南北为一。
sentences.m: 先前院中是南北相通的一个整体。
sentences.e: Formerly the courtyard ran through from north to south as one whole.

sentences.c: 迨诸父异爨，内外多置小门墙，往往而是。
sentences.m: 等到伯父叔父们分了家各自起灶做饭，里里外外设置了许多小门和隔墙，到处都是。
sentences.e: Then my uncles divided the household and kept separate kitchens, and small doors and partition walls were put up inside and out, until they were everywhere.

sentences.c: 东犬西吠，客逾庖而宴，鸡栖于厅。
sentences.m: 东家的狗对着西家叫，客人得越过厨房去赴宴，鸡在厅堂里栖息。
sentences.e: Dogs in the east barked at those in the west, guests had to pass through the kitchen to reach the feast, and chickens roosted in the hall.

sentences.c: 庭中始为篱，已为墙，凡再变矣。
sentences.m: 院中先是编篱笆，后来筑成墙，一共变了两次。
sentences.e: At first the courtyard was divided by a fence, later by a wall — twice changed in all.

sentences.c: 家有老妪，尝居于此。
sentences.m: 家里有个老妇人，曾经住在这里。
sentences.e: There was an old woman in the house who had once lived here.

sentences.c: 妪，先大母婢也，乳二世，先妣抚之甚厚。
sentences.m: 这老妇人是已故祖母的婢女，做过两代人的乳母，已故的母亲待她很优厚。
sentences.e: She had been my late grandmother's maid and had nursed two generations; my late mother treated her very kindly.

sentences.c: 室西连于中闺，先妣尝一至。
sentences.m: 屋子的西边连着内室，母亲曾经来过一次。
sentences.e: The room's west side joined the inner apartments, and my mother had come there once.

sentences.c: 妪每谓余曰：「某所，而母立于兹。」
sentences.m: 老妇人常对我说：「这个地方，你母亲曾站在那里。」
sentences.e: The old woman would often say to me, "This is the spot where your mother stood."

sentences.c: 妪又曰：「汝姊在吾怀，呱呱而泣；娘以指叩门扉曰：『儿寒乎？欲食乎？』吾从板外相为应答。」
sentences.m: 老妇人又说：「你姐姐在我怀里，呱呱地哭；你娘用手指敲着门板问：『孩子冷吗？想吃东西吗？』我就在门板外面一一回答。」
sentences.e: She would add: "Your elder sister was in my arms, crying; your mother tapped on the door with her finger and asked, 'Is the child cold? Does she want something to eat?' and I answered her from the other side of the boards."

sentences.c: 语未毕，余泣，妪亦泣。
sentences.m: 话还没说完，我哭了，老妇人也哭了。
sentences.e: Before she finished speaking I was weeping, and so was she.

sentences.c: 余自束发读书轩中，一日，大母过余曰：「吾儿，久不见若影，何竟日默默在此，大类女郎也？」
sentences.m: 我从十五岁起在轩中读书，有一天，祖母来看我，说：「我的孩子，好久没见到你的身影了，为什么整天默默地待在这里，真像个女孩子呀？」
sentences.e: From the time I tied up my hair and began studying in the chamber, my grandmother came to me one day and said: "My child, I have not seen you for so long — why do you sit here silent all day long, just like a girl?"

sentences.c: 比去，以手阖门，自语曰：「吾家读书久不效，儿之成，则可待乎！」
sentences.m: 等到离开时，她用手关上房门，自言自语说：「我们家读书长久没有成效，这孩子的成就，总该可以期待吧！」
sentences.e: As she left she closed the door with her hand and said to herself: "Our family has studied so long without result — surely this boy's success may be looked for!"

sentences.c: 顷之，持一象笏至，曰：「此吾祖太常公宣德间执此以朝，他日汝当用之！」
sentences.m: 过了一会儿，她拿着一块象笏走来，说：「这是我的祖父太常公在宣德年间拿着上朝用的，将来你应当用它！」
sentences.e: A little later she came back holding an ivory tablet and said: "This is what my grandfather, the Minister of Rites, carried to court in the Xuande years — one day you shall use it!"

sentences.c: 瞻顾遗迹，如在昨日，令人长号不自禁。
sentences.m: 回想这些旧事，就像发生在昨天，让人忍不住放声痛哭。
sentences.e: Looking back on those traces, it is as if it were yesterday, and I cannot keep myself from crying aloud.

sentences.c: 轩东故尝为厨，人往，从轩前过。
sentences.m: 轩的东边从前做过厨房，人们到那里去，都从轩前经过。
sentences.e: East of the chamber there had once been a kitchen, and people going there passed in front of it.

sentences.c: 余扃牖而居，久之，能以足音辨人。
sentences.m: 我关着窗户住在里面，时间久了，能凭脚步声分辨出是谁。
sentences.e: I lived with the windows shut, and in time I could tell who was coming by the sound of their steps.

sentences.c: 轩凡四遭火，得不焚，殆有神护者。
sentences.m: 轩一共四次遭遇火灾，都没有被烧毁，大概有神灵保护吧。
sentences.e: The chamber caught fire four times in all and was never burned down; perhaps some spirit protected it.

sentences.c: 余既为此志，后五年，吾妻来归，时至轩中，从余问古事，或凭几学书。
sentences.m: 我写了这篇志之后，过了五年，我的妻子嫁到我家来，时常到轩中来，向我问些古代的事，或者靠着书案学写字。
sentences.e: Five years after I wrote this account, my wife came to our house; she would often come into the chamber, ask me about things of the past, or lean on the desk and practice writing.

sentences.c: 吾妻归宁，述诸小妹语曰：「闻姊家有阁子，且何谓阁子也？」
sentences.m: 我的妻子回娘家省亲，转述她妹妹们的话说：「听说姐姐家有阁子，那么什么叫阁子呢？」
sentences.e: When my wife went home to visit her family, she repeated what her younger sisters had said: "We hear our sister's house has a pavilion — and what is a pavilion?"

sentences.c: 其后六年，吾妻死，室坏不修。
sentences.m: 此后六年，我的妻子死了，屋子坏了也没有修。
sentences.e: Six years after that my wife died, and the room fell into disrepair and was not mended.

sentences.c: 其后二年，余久卧病无聊，乃使人复葺南阁子，其制稍异于前。
sentences.m: 此后两年，我长久卧病，十分无聊，就派人重新修整南阁子，格局和从前稍有不同。
sentences.e: Two years later, having lain ill a long while and grown weary of it, I had the South Pavilion repaired again; its form was a little different from before.

sentences.c: 然自后余多在外，不常居。
sentences.m: 然而从那以后我大多在外面，不常住了。
sentences.e: But from then on I was mostly away and did not often live there.

sentences.c: 庭有枇杷树，吾妻死之年所手植也，今已亭亭如盖矣。
sentences.m: 院中有一棵枇杷树，是我妻子死的那年她亲手种的，如今已经高高挺立、枝叶像伞盖一样了。
sentences.e: In the courtyard stands a loquat tree that she planted with her own hands the year my wife died; now it rises tall and its crown spreads like a canopy.
